entities.name: Alonso de Alvarado
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Alonso de Alvarado Montaya González de Cevallos y Miranda (1500–1556) was a prominent Spanish conquistador whose campaigns profoundly shaped the early colonial administration of Peru and the Andean region during the mid-16th century. A knight of the prestigious Order of Santiago, Alvarado served under Francisco Pizarro, playing a crucial role in consolidating Spanish control over the former Inca Empire and suppressing indigenous resistance and internal Spanish rebellions. His career spanned the tumultuous period immediately following the conquest, marked by intense territorial disputes and the establishment of new viceregal structures, making him a central figure in the violent transition from Inca rule to Spanish dominion.

Alvarado arrived in the New World in 1534, joining Francisco Pizarro's forces in Peru shortly after the capture of Cuzco. He quickly distinguished himself through military leadership, most notably in 1537 when Pizarro dispatched him to relieve his brother Hernando Pizarro, who was besieged by Manco Inca's forces in Cuzco. Alvarado subsequently commanded forces against Diego de Almagro during the first civil war among the conquistadors, securing a decisive victory for Pizarro's faction at the Battle of Las Salinas in 1538. He later participated in the suppression of the Great Inca Rebellion and was instrumental in the establishment of the Audiencia of Lima, serving as its first president. His administrative and military efforts were critical in laying the groundwork for the Viceroyalty of Peru, particularly in the northern territories, where he undertook expeditions into the Chachapoyas region.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Alonso de Alvarado's military and administrative contributions were crucial in stabilizing the early Spanish colonial regime in Peru, suppressing both indigenous revolts and internal conquistador conflicts. His actions solidified Spanish control over the former Inca Empire and helped lay the institutional foundations for the Viceroyalty of Peru.
